newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: IMF tells Sierra Leone to raise fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: IMF tells Sierra Leone to raise fuel prices.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is demanding fuel and energy price rises in Sierra Leone as a condition for continuing funding in the impoverished West African nation, finance ministry officials said on Wednesday.

But Finance Minister Thaimu Bangura, in remarks quoted by state radio on Tuesday, said that the government was asking IMF to consider its economic, social and political problems in drawing up a new programme.
"The IMF is demanding the government increase the pump price of petrol, kerosene, fuel oil and also electricity tariffs. These are IMF conditionalities for Sierra Leone," one official told Reuters.

IMF programmes aim to cut budget deficits, in part often due to subsidies on such sensitive items as food or fuel. The IMF target date for the price increases was the end of March, the officials said.
The radio quoted Bangura as saying that the government ... "will not introduce any measure that will lead to explosive situations in the country".
Sierra Leone is struggling to emerge from five years of civil war.

President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who took office in March 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule, signed a peace deal with rebels in Ivory Coast in November but implementation has dragged.
